title: The conclusion of the elimination theorem, as a predicate on the data
statement:
Let $S$ be qcqs, let $X$ and $Y$ be qcqs $S$-schemes with $Y\to S$ separated and of finite type, let $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$ be dense open subschemes whose open immersions into $X$ are quasi-compact, let $p\colon Y\to X$ be a morphism and let $f\colon U\to Y$ be a section of $p$ over $U$. We say that *the conclusion of the elimination theorem holds for the data $(X,U,V,p,f)$* when there exist a $V$-admissible blow-up $\pi\colon\widetilde X\to X$ ([def-nagata-admissible-blowup]) and a quasi-domination $(W,g)$ of $\widetilde X$ over $Y$ relative to $S$ ([def-nagata-conrad-quasi-domination]), where $\widetilde X$ has its $S$-structure through $\pi$, such that $\pi^{-1}(U)\subseteq W$ and

$$
g|_{\pi^{-1}(U)}=f\circ\pi_U,\qquad
\pi_U\colon\pi^{-1}(U)\to U.
$$

Here $\pi_U$ is the restriction of $\pi$. Thus the extension condition compares morphisms with the same source, the inverse image of $U$ in the blow-up.
